segments.title: Castles as instruments of sea power
segments.summary: A planned study of the Welsh castle ring asks how access to the sea shaped fortification strategy and design.
segments.body: The planned Long Patrol examines the ring of stone castles used to pacify Wales through a maritime lens. It asks how the realities of the sea affected the castles' purpose and design. The argument reaches back to Roman times and follows the idea forward through the Welsh castle-building program. A science-fiction comparison considers whether bases work better on moons, large satellites, or asteroids than on a planet's surface. The passage previews the strategic question behind the longer castle series.

evidence.note: Clarke announces a castle series on the maritime logic of fortifications used to pacify Wales, with Roman and science-fiction comparisons.
